assessment.nobel_worthiness: Established political economics as a field, using formal models and empirical work to show how electoral rules, constitutions, state capacity and fiscal institutions shape policy and long-run development. It is foundational and changed how economists treat institutions, and it connects well with the historical and comparative literature.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the clearest core, with their joint monograph and papers on electoral rules and constitutions. Besley is a close third through state capacity, accountability and development-politics work. A trio fits the list, though other contributors such as Acemoglu, Robinson and Alesina are outside this ballot entry or already recognised.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with three decades of cumulative work, many replications and extensions, and wide use in empirical political economy and economic history. The timing is ripe.
uncertainties: The 2024 prize on institutions may make the committee cautious about a closely adjacent topic.
Whether the committee would define the prize narrowly around constitutions and electoral rules or more broadly around state capacity.
I have not independently verified citation or priority details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Melitz's 2003 model of heterogeneous firms, selection and trade is among the most influential theoretical advances in trade since Krugman. It changed how economists think about the gains from trade, reallocation across firms and the margins of adjustment, and it linked theory to firm-level data.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the central originator. Helpman has a distinct, broad record, including firm-level trade with Melitz and Yeaple and the earlier increasing-returns trade theory. Redding is a major contributor to quantitative and spatial extensions but is more junior. Proposing two names keeps credit concentrated.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with more than twenty years of firm-level evidence, structural applications and policy use. Robust to the rise of quantitative trade models.
uncertainties: Krugman's 2008 prize covered related trade ground, so the committee may see the contribution as an extension of an already-recognised field.
Overlap with Helpman in the trade-policy entry, and a possible alternative pairing with Grossman.
Whether Redding's quantitative work should be credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Combined technology and trade-shock research reshaped understanding of labour-market adjustment, wage inequality, regional decline and the political fallout of globalisation. It is empirically rigorous, uses local-labour-market variation, and bears on current questions about automation and trade. It matches the concern, voiced publicly by committee members, with how societies absorb technological change.
assessment.attribution: The China-shock work is clearly Autor, Dorn and Hanson. The task-based and skill-bias framework involves Autor, Katz and others, and Acemoglu has already been recognised for related ideas. A trio from the trade-shock line is defensible, but it leaves out Katz and the task-model originators.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature, with a decade-plus of replication, extensions and debate. Some findings have been refined by later work on persistence and the political effects.
uncertainties: The 2024 and 2025 prizes touched adjacent themes, which may crowd out a closely related award.
Credit is split between the tasks and skill-bias strand and the China-shock strand.
Debate over the size and persistence of the effects.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Kiyotaki-Moore model of credit cycles shows how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks. It is a foundational mechanism in macro-finance, widely used after the global financial crisis and in the modern analysis of financial frictions.
assessment.attribution: The 1997 paper is a clean, well-defined two-person contribution. Gertler and Gilchrist's financial accelerator work is a complementary strand, with Bernanke's prize in 2022 already recognising related ideas. Two names keep the proposal tight.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with nearly thirty years of influence on theory, policy models and empirical financial-friction work.
uncertainties: The 2022 prize on banks and financial crises may make the committee see this area as partly recognised.
Whether the committee would prefer to include Gertler or Gilchrist.
The contribution is more theoretical and less directly empirical than some others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Used linked administrative data at population scale to measure intergenerational mobility, show its geographic variation and identify place-based and childhood-exposure effects. It transformed empirical public economics and the measurement of opportunity, and it is the kind of data-building plus causal design I value.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear leader and the principal driver of the data and methods. Hendren and Friedman are central co-authors on exposure effects and mobility, and Katz is also credited. Attribution within large collaborations is harder to separate.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature. The core results date from the mid-2010s and have drawn replication and extension, but some conclusions (for example on neighbourhood causal effects) are still being tested.
uncertainties: A younger career than most alternatives, so the committee may wait.
Large collaborative teams complicate the three-name limit.
Open debate on identification of place effects and the stability of the estimates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Developed the empirical tools, including BLP demand estimation and dynamic industry models, that underpin modern merger analysis, competition policy and applied industrial organisation. Methodological impact is large and the tools are routinely used in practice.
assessment.attribution: The BLP trio (Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes) is a natural group, and Pakes has an additional dynamic-oversight contribution (Ericson-Pakes). Bresnahan and Reiss are important alternatives with earlier empirical-IO roots, so credit is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature. The methods have been in routine use for about thirty years and are embedded in antitrust and regulatory work.
uncertainties: Prior recognition of related ground (Tirole, and Heckman and McFadden on discrete choice) may reduce the committee's appetite.
Which of Bresnahan, Pakes or others best fits the three-name cap.
Methodological rather than question-driven discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework, with nominal rigidities, the Taylor rule and the modern theory of monetary policy, is the dominant paradigm in central banks. Its practical influence on policy design and inflation targeting is very large.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across many contributors, including Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and Gertler. The three-name cap forces hard choices, and the intellectual lineage includes earlier laureates (Phelps, Lucas, Sargent, Sims, Kydland-Prescott).
assessment.maturity: Very mature. Decades of use in policy and teaching, although the 2008 crisis and post-2021 inflation prompted rethinking and the rise of heterogeneous-agent models.
uncertainties: Diffuse attribution across a large group.
Possible shift of the field toward heterogeneous-agent frameworks.
Political and policy association of the Taylor rule.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification changed how economists reason about what data can and cannot reveal, bringing transparent treatment of uncertainty and weak assumptions into empirical work. Manski's foundational contributions on bounds, selection and treatment-response are conceptually deep.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the clear originator. Tamer and Molinari developed the inferential and applied machinery (moment inequalities, econometric theory). A pair or a trio is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Mature in theory, with decades of development. Applied adoption is real but narrower than that of mainstream point-identified methods.
uncertainties: Methodological contributions have a smaller footprint on mainstream empirical practice than some competitors.
Econometrics has received recent recognition, so the committee may rotate to other fields.
Whether Manski's age and the breadth of his work favour an earlier award.
